newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gives provisional nod to Albania elections.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives provisional nod to Albania elections.

text.p: The United States gave a provisional clean bill of health on Monday to Albania's weekend general election but said it would leave a final assessment to a team of international monitors.

The State Department declined comment on the result of the election -- an apparent win for the opposition Socialist Party -- and refused to speculate on whether heavily criticised President Sali Berisha would or should resign as a result.
Spokesman John Dinger said reports of violence in some parts of the country "didn't appear to indicate widepread problems that affected the overall (election) process."
The vote-counting process "was complicated and sometimes contentious, but seemed to be within the boundaries of overall international standards," Dinger told reporters.

Dinger said that for a definitive ruling the United States would await a judgment by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which observed the vote along with a 100-strong U.S. delegation.
"We do want to make clear, however, that the initial reports indicate that this was clear evidence that the people of Albania want to return to the democratic process," he said.
"So if there's a winner in this election, apart from the candidates, it will certainly be the Albanian people," he said.
Earlier Catherine Lalumiere, who headed the OSCE observers, said that despite some problems "we can say that the elections can be considered as adequate and acceptable."

The Socialists claimed that they had won almost two thirds of the seats in parliament, a majority that would allow them to remove the head of state. Berisha has given no indication whether he will resign.

Berisha has been been widely blamed for the anarchy that has reigned in parts of Albania for much of this year. More than 1,500 people have been killed in violence sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes in January.
